title: SiteScope — Atlas Instance Configuration
description: A SiteScope represents a distinct Resilience Atlas instance (e.g. a country, theme, or program). Each site scope has its own subdomain, layers, layer groups, and settings.
list_endpoint: Agent tool: get_site_scopes (preferred). Raw admin API fallback: GET /api/admin/layers/site_scopes.

key_fields.id: Integer primary key. Always use this to link layers and scope_datasets.
key_fields.name: Display name (translated). E.g. 'Resilience Atlas', 'LDN Uganda'.
key_fields.subdomain: URL subdomain that identifies this site. E.g. 'ldn', 'trendsearth', 'indicators'. The main site uses subdomain null or 'default'.
key_fields.has_analysis: Boolean. Enables the analysis panel (allows indicator analysis on selected areas).
key_fields.latitude: Float. Map center latitude on load.
key_fields.longitude: Float. Map center longitude on load.
key_fields.color: Hex accent color for this site, e.g. '#C62828'.
key_fields.header_color: Hex color for the header background.
key_fields.logo_url: URL to the site logo image.
key_fields.analysis_options: Boolean. Enables advanced analysis options panel.
key_fields.has_gef_logo: Boolean. Shows GEF logo in header.

usage_notes: When creating a layer, always specify the site_scope_id to link it to the correct site.
site_scope_id is passed as a top-level param: POST /api/admin/layers with {"site_scope_id": <id>, "layer": {...}}.
Scope datasets are linked to a site_scope via site_scope_id.
Layer groups belong to a single site_scope.
The raw admin API for listing groups in a site scope is GET /api/admin/layer_groups?site_scope_id=<id>.
To find the correct site_scope_id, use get_site_scopes. Do not ask the user for a numeric ID unless there is no resolvable name.
how_to_find_site_scope_id: Use get_site_scopes. It returns [{id, name, subdomain}]. The main default site is typically id=1 in existing environments, but the agent should still resolve by name rather than hard-coding IDs.
